items.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 23 at 2:59AM EDT until September 23 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
items.description:
* WHAT...Strong north to south longshore current. There is also a
Moderate Risk of rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Pender and Coastal New Hanover Counties.

* WHEN...Today.

* IMPACTS...Longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers
into rip currents, piers, jetties, and other hazardous areas.
It may sweep swimmers off their feet, making it difficult to
return to shore.
items.instruction:
Caution should be used when in or near the water. Check with
lifeguards before entering the ocean for possible hazards you may
be swept into.

items.headline: Gale Watch issued September 23 at 2:20AM EDT until September 25 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Small Craft Advisory, northeast winds 15 to 25
kt with gusts up to 30 kt and seas 5 to 8 ft. For the Gale
Watch, north winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 35 kt and seas
6 to 9 ft possible.

* WHERE...Southeast North Carolina coastal waters out 20 NM.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 2 PM EDT Thursday.
For the Gale Watch, from Thursday afternoon through late
Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds can cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
items.instruction:
Mariners should consider altering plans to avoid possible
hazardous conditions.  Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter
course, and/or secure the vessel for severe wind and seas.
